title: Opaque Types with some
hints: `some Drawable` returns one specific hidden type.
`makeTriangle` returns a `Triangle`; `flipped` wraps its argument in a generic `Flipped<D: Drawable>` that reverses the lines.
jsBridge: `some Drawable` means "one specific type I'm not telling you". The compiler knows it, callers don't. It's how SwiftUI's `some View` works. TS has no equivalent: returning an interface type loses the concrete type entirely, which is `any` in Swift terms.

compass.q: TS returning `Drawable` = Swift's `any Drawable`. What does `some Drawable` keep that `any` loses (static type, performance)?
`some View` vs `AnyView`: why does Apple warn against `AnyView`?
Why can't a `some Drawable` function return a `Triangle` on one branch and a `Square` on another?
Every SwiftUI `body` is `some View`. What is its real type for a `VStack` with two `Text`s?
